research_thread.scientific_problem: Overcoming the trade-off between castability, segregation, and strength-ductility balance in high-entropy alloys for high-temperature applications.
research_thread.sample_lineage: Commercially pure raw materials -> Conventional casting -> 2.5 kg bulk ingot
research_thread.intervention: Application of the Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy (EHEA) design strategy (mixing soft fcc and hard bcc phases).
research_thread.baseline: Conventional HEAs (inferior castability, segregation, strength-ductility conflict) and NiAl-based eutectics (low RT ductility, expensive processing).
research_thread.conditions: Conventional casting, room temperature to 700°C testing
research_thread.outcome: Unprecedented combination of high fracture strength, high ductility, and good castability in a 2.5 kg ingot.
research_thread.mechanism: Fine lamellar structure stores dislocations effectively; alternating soft/hard phases provide work hardening.
research_thread.hypothesis_value: Using eutectic solidification principles in HEAs can simultaneously achieve near-equilibrium microstructures (solving castability) and composite strengthening (solving strength-ductility).
alternative_explanations: The properties might be unique to this specific composition and not transferable to other pseudo-binary systems.
